title: ‘So wrong’: Expert slams US economists who claimed tariffs would cause inflation spike
summary: Sky News Australia (Feb 2026): economist says US tariffs produced no inflation spike or recession, raise hundreds of billions the Treasury needs, and the US is among the fastest-growing OECD economies.

assertions.quote: there'd be a big spike in inflation in the US because of the tariffs and it's just simply not happened.

verdicts.note: Headline CPI stayed near 2.5-3 percent through 2025 rather than spiking, but core goods prices turned up and studies attribute several tenths of a point to tariffs; most forecasts were for a one-off 1-2 point level rise.

Tariffs lifted consumer goods inflation in the sample from slightly negative to about 2 percent, a 2.9 point contribution spread over a year rather than a sudden spike; the post does not compare this to any economist forecasts and covers goods only.

assertions.quote: it raises 300 three or400 billion a year. That's a massive amount of money

verdicts.note: Customs receipts ran about 30 billion dollars a month in late 2025, roughly 5 percent of federal revenue and several times the pre-2025 level.

assertions.quote: Well that's why the economists have been so wrong because they clearly haven't.

verdicts.note: US GDP grew about 2 percent in 2025 with no recession, though estimates put the tariff drag at a few tenths of a point.

Private employment grew every quarter of 2025 (134.7 million in January to 135.1 million in December) and unemployment stayed between 4.0% and 4.5%, so no recession occurred in 2025; the series say nothing about tariffs' role either way.

assertions.quote: one of the fastest growing economists in the OECD

verdicts.note: US growth near 2 percent in 2025 led the G7 and beat the OECD average of about 1.5 percent.
